Cell 001: n list, coded

The sorted list of every Carmichael number n, split into residue classes modulo 10,810,800. Each class is stored by binary interpolative coding.

Switches: A off, B off, C on. What the switches mean.

Times are on an Intel Core i9-9900K (8 cores, 16 threads), 64 GB RAM, NVMe SSD, Windows 10. Decode times are in memory. The notes under the results table say how each time is measured.

Build

Rebuild the file from the oracle with:

make fetch-oracle rebuild-001

The target first builds the n list (see intermediate files), then runs the encoder:

nstats_orc1 data/carmichael-1e24-oracle.orc1 --emit-n work/n.raw --emit-only
list_build classes work/n.raw work/carmichael-1e24-cell001-n-classes.cnd --mod 10810800 --targets-self

Verify, decode and certify

make fetch-001 verify-001
make fetch-oracle certify-001

Verify first checks the size and SHA-256 of the file. Then the targets run these commands:

# make verify-001
list_decode data/carmichael-1e24-cell001-n-classes.cnd
# make certify-001
list_decode data/carmichael-1e24-cell001-n-classes.cnd --kind n --certify data/carmichael-1e24-oracle.orc1 --threads N
# make decode-001
list_decode data/carmichael-1e24-cell001-n-classes.cnd --emit work/c001.values.raw

N is the number of threads. The reproduce page explains the folders and the defaults.
